title: Huawei, once hobbled by US sanctions, passes 100 million Kirin chip milestone
key_facts: Huawei announced on 13 Oct 2026 that it has shipped more than 100 million Kirin-powered devices since 2023.
Huawei has not disclosed a breakdown of the 100 million devices by model, processor generation or market.
Huawei gave details of the Kirin 9050 series, which it calls the first mass-produced chip to use its proprietary LogicFolding architecture, developed under a framework known as the Tau Scaling Law.
The chip uses more than 50 million hybrid bonds and Huawei reports a 53.5% improvement in transistor density.
Huawei said the Kirin 9050 series reached mass production with the support of China's domestic electronics supply chain.
Tech Edition says the announcement does not independently show how the chip compares with rivals; independent testing would be needed.
Tech Edition cites Chinese outlet Yicai (13 Oct) saying testing of the next-generation Kirin 2027 has begun.
quote_evidence: Huawei Technologies has shipped more than 100 million devices powered by its Kirin processors since 2023, marking a significant step in its efforts to rebuild its semiconductor business despite US export restrictions.
However, the company has not disclosed a detailed breakdown of the 100 million devices by model, processor generation or individual market.
“The Kirin 9050 series has successfully achieved mass production with the support of China’s domestic electronics supply chain,” the company said.
why_it_matters_hint: Huawei can keep making its own phone chips under US sanctions, according to its own figures.
notes: SCMP original blocked (403); Huawei Central also blocked. Tech Edition text read. All figures are Huawei's own claims. Our 1 Oct edition carried the launch of Huawei phones with the Kirin 9050 Pro and LogicFolding.
